720	The head knows what is right and wrong.
721	Right? For example, a person about to commit a transgression
722	usually knows he is about to commit a transgression. Because of
723	that he looks right and left. Why? Because the mind
724	knows it is not good. But why does he commit
725	the transgression? Because the heart craves. The heart has desire.
726	So if you are a king, with the mind ruling the heart, the mind
727	defeats the heart. But if you are a Lemech, first comes lust,
728	and only afterwards the intellect, then you are like the nations. So what does He
729	say to him? "And He will give their kings into your hand": whatever you call
730	their way, which is the way of Lemech, will be yours,
731	you will rule over it. Another thing:
732	Why does He give the kings? So that you know that if
733	the king falls,
734	the whole people falls after him. Right? How would He make
735	his minister fall in heaven? The moment Moshe Rabbeinu saw the minister
736	of Og thrown down on the ground, he understood they had already
737	lost. The moment it is cast down in heaven onto the ground, the whole
738	people will lose. Same thing here on earth. The people see the
739	king fall, they all surrender and do not fight. How do
740	we know? In Yehoshua it is written: "And they brought out these kings
741	to Yehoshua." They won, they brought the kings
742	to Yehoshua. "And Yehoshua called all the men of Israel and said
743	to the commanders of the men of war who went with him: Come near, put
744	your feet on the necks of these kings." He had the
745	kings lie down, and all the commanders of Israel put their
746	foot on their throats, which is the sign of humiliation and submission,
747	and it was fulfilled exactly as it is written here: "And He will give their kings
748	into your hand." Exactly. You see, something promised here
749	did indeed happen.
750	What does He say now? He says this: "The graven images of their gods
751	you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver and gold on them
752	and take it for yourself." Why? "Lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to
753	HaShem your Elokim." That is, you arrive and conquer
754	their village, and there is plunder. Part of what they had was
755	idols of idolatry. Now, what would they do?
756	They would make the idol perhaps of wood
757	or stone, but decorate it with gold jewelry.
758	So He says: first of all, burn their idols.
759	But what about the silver and gold? What a pity, there is silver and gold,
760	good, we can melt it down, maybe make rings
761	and bracelets for a woman, something. The Holy One, blessed be He, says: do not
762	covet the silver and gold on them. What is on the idols you also
763	burn and destroy. Why? "Lest you be snared by it," like a land mine. Even
764	if you melt it down, it will always nag in your head that it once
765	was idolatry, and in the end it might make you fall
766	and somehow you will serve it. So He says "lest you be snared." You don't know.
767	You say, "No, I am strong." You cannot be
768	strong, you don't know. There once was an inclination
769	for idolatry, like a man is forbidden to be alone with
770	a woman who is not his wife, what is called yichud, so that
771	you don't know. Do not say "I am strong." "There is no
772	guardian over lions," the Sages say. You don't know
773	how it will make you fall. The same with idolatry.
774	The Sages abolished the inclination for idolatry. We do not
775	understand this today, but once there was a very strong inclination
776	for idolatry. So He says you don't know
777	how it will make you fall, so
778	destroy it. Why? "For it is an abomination to HaShem your Elokim."
779	"And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you be
780	devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest it and abhor it, for it is devoted."
781	What does He say? Do not bring an abomination into your house and do not bring in any
782	thing connected to idolatry into your house. Where does this apply
783	today? There are poor people who don't know,
784	who come back from the East and bring statues of this Buddha,
785	what's his name? They bring statues like these of
786	idolatry. They put them in the house for decoration. All kinds of
787	things used for idolatry in the Far East, they put
788	these statues of this Buddha, and they think
789	it's decoration, but it is idolatry.
790	"Do not bring idolatry into your house." So wait, a person
791	will say, what's the problem? Do I bow to it? Do I
792	worship it? It's just decoration. Tell me, if now
793	the police come to someone's house, do a search, and find
794	there a machine for printing dollars,
795	he says, "But I didn't print dollars, I only
796	keep the machine." They will say, "Ah, fine, so you're
797	fine, you're a giant." Of course not! And a lab,
798	equipment for producing drugs, he says, "But I didn't
799	produce drugs." "But sir, you have prohibited equipment here."
800	So you see, even if you did not commit
801	the transgression, the very fact that you keep the tools to commit
802	the transgression, you will be punished for that too in court. Right?
803	Same thing. Why do you bring idolatry home? You
804	say, "But I didn't worship it." So what is it doing in your
805	house? Whoever doesn't know, poor thing, that is why
806	we listen to a Torah class. Everyone should go through the house,
807	check whether he has something resembling idolatry, all kinds of
808	statues, all kinds of unrelated things, throw it out of
809	the house. Why do you need it? On the Day of Judgment
810	you will give an account for such a thing. HaShem have mercy. Some
811	say "do not bring an abomination into your house" refers to the
812	beautiful woman, that if you go to war and see a beautiful
813	gentile woman, even though the Torah, under very, very, very
814	strict conditions, permitted her to you,
815	they say, do not bring an abomination into your house.
816	Now what else is "do not bring an abomination into your house
817	and you will be devoted to destruction like it"? Cherem is the letters of chomer, right,
818	without the vav, so that you not be far from HaShem, with a spirit,
819	with materiality without spirituality. Because what is cherem? Cherem is
820	matter. Matter distances you from HaShem. Cherem is also
821	the letters of Ramach: if you bring an abomination, it will bring
822	troubles on your 248 limbs. And cherem is also the letters of rachem,
823	for whoever repents, and removes it
824	from the house, HaShem has mercy on him. So you see how many
825	hints. Now what else does He say to him? "All the commandments that
826	I command you today you shall keep to do, so that you may live,
827	multiply, and come and possess the land that HaShem swore
828	to your fathers." That is, what does He say to him?
829	"So that you may live and multiply." That is, see, the Torah
830	is a Torah of life, and the Holy One, blessed be He, promises
831	that fulfilling the mitzvot brings a person vitality. Wait, but
832	someone will say, wait, I know some who don't
833	keep anything, and they live. I know one who violates
834	all the transgressions, eats pork, eats this,
835	desecrates Shabbat, and lives, right? He is physically alive like
836	a cow, like a dog, a dog also lives, a cow also lives. But
837	what? They live physically, but he has no spiritual
838	vitality. Vitality is a spiritual matter, and it continues
